subject: raw food and cooking
title: What If You Never Ate Cooked Food Again?

scenes.text: What if you never ate cooked food again? You could eat all day and still go hungry.
Your gut gets only about half the energy out of raw starch. From cooked starch, it gets nearly all of it.
To make up the gap, you'd chew like a great ape: five or six hours a day.
Within months, weight drops. In a German study of about two hundred raw-food eaters, up to a third were underweight.
On long-term raw diets, about half of women stop having periods, a sign the body is running short of energy.
No hunter-gatherer group ever studied eats all its food raw. Cooking may be the thing that made us human.

description:
What if you never ate cooked food again? Harvard anthropologist Richard Wrangham notes we get about half the energy from raw starch but nearly all from cooked starch, and that chewing like great apes would take five or six hours a day.
In a Giessen study of about 200 raw-food eaters, a quarter to a third were underweight, and many women on strict raw diets stop menstruating. No known hunter-gatherer group eats all its food raw.
